 Princess Anne has just played a blinder — the Argentines are fuming
 OPINION: Express reporter Adam Toms has been left thrilled by Princess Anne's visit to the Falkland Islands.
 Share Article Share Article Facebook X LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Email Copy Link Link copied Add us as preferred source Comments OPINION By  Adam Toms 15:33, Thu, Nov 19, 2026 Updated: 15:38, Thu, Nov 19, 2026 
 Princess Anne has visited the South Atlantic (Image: Getty) Princess Anne is the most popular member of the Royal Family , and rightly so. Who could fail to be touched by the way she stayed with her mother, Her Late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, in her final hours, and while her coffin was transported down to London from Balmoral? She has carried out her royal duties over the decades with a stoic distinction, and even represented Britain in the Olympics, let’s not forget. YouGov says she has a 67% popularity rating, pipping Catherine, the Princess of Wales , to first place in the table, who is on 64%. The Princess Royal has yet again proven she is a great asset to her country by visiting the Falkland Islands and South Georgia with her husband, Vice Admiral Sir Timothy Laurence.
 She stopped by in her capacity as Patron of the South Georgia Heritage Trust. South Georgia was invaded by Argentina in 1982 before troops landed in Stanley, the capital of the Falklands. The former has no permanent human inhabitants due to inclement conditions, but is home to loads of penguins.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Among other things, she formally opened the new National Sports Complex in Stanley and commemorated the explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton. Her mere presence has rattled the Argentines, with Buenos Aires denouncing her visit as a "provocation”.
 This was of course by no means the purpose of her dropping by, but it is a side effect that triggered a smirk on my face. A senior royal setting foot on what is British soil sends a very clear message — the Falklands are British, want to stay British and will not be intimidated.

 Argentina has thrown its toys out of the pram and kicked up a stink in recent months after Donald Trump suggested that the United States could change its stance over the islands. They have tried to halt oil extraction in surrounding waters, but the £1.55billion Sea Lion project is pushing ahead as planned in the face of "illegitimate threats”.
 Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT I hope Her Royal Highness enjoyed her time in the Falklands. This was by no means her first time. It is a special place, which I had the pleasure of seeing myself earlier this year .

 Prince Harry finally breaks silence over shock return as a working royal 
 The Princess Royal opened a sports centre in Stanley (Image: Getty) Its people will not be intimidated by bullies seeking to overturn their will. They have no hope of doing so anyway, as the British government continues to rightly say the future of the islands is in the hands of the islanders themselves, and the princess’s visit has made this crystal clear once again.
